items.good: The builder and the approver meet the template's headings in its order: the title, how the tool is put together with a link to the README where the UX is defined, its own principles each in a line, User stories, Architecture with a Logical view (the figure in architecture.svg shown as an image, then the lines it cannot show) and a Physical view (a tree, then what the tool depends on and how it starts), and Test, which, as the user chose, says the project has no rules for checks and gives what this tool's checks need; each list line is one sentence, its why after a blank line indented under it, nothing in bold.

From the opening the reader tells how the tool is put together, a Planner deciding where each file goes, a Mover carrying it out while a Record keeper keeps each move outside the folder, and an Undoer putting back the last move, and the five principles every decision is held to: never deleting, renaming or overwriting, moving only the files directly in the folder, adding nothing inside it but the kinds' folders, deciding where each file goes in one place, and installing by downloading one file; it is built on no other architecture, which it says.

Every scene of the README rests on one of four stories, each one way the user runs the tool: listing with nothing moved (on ~/Downloads or another folder), moving, undoing the last move, and seeing how to run it; none is a step inside the tool or named by a technology.

The reader follows each story through the figure's arrows and the lines in the order they act: to list, the Command line asks the Planner, which reads the names in the folder and in its kinds' folders, so it can say a name is taken; to move, the same plan goes to the Mover, which moves files and adds each file moved through the Record keeper; to undo, the Undoer reads the last move and moves files back; help is printed. The choices a builder or approver would question are given with why: recording each file as it is moved, moving by a hard link so a taken name is never overwritten (checked: os.link onto a taken name raises FileExistsError and leaves both files, os.rename replaces it), and, on a drive that cannot make hard links such as a FAT or exFAT USB stick, moving by making the new file only where the name is free, copying, then removing the old name, or removing the new file again where the copy fails, so the move story is achieved on any folder the README lets the user name and no file is added (checked: open in 'x' mode on a taken name raises FileExistsError and leaves it as it was).

From the tree the builder tells that every component of the figure is in the one Python 3 script using the standard library alone, that the tests sit under organize-downloads/tests, that the script is installed to ~/.local/bin, and that the record is a JSON Lines file per folder in ~/.local/state/organize-downloads/ on Linux or ~/Library/Application Support/organize-downloads/ on macOS; the lines say the tool depends on Python alone and is started as organize-downloads, handed to python3 by its first line.

As the user chose, the Test section says the project has no rules for checks and gives this tool's: each component by unittest tests, each a Given, a When and a Then, each user story by running the script on a temporary test folder with a temporary home folder, all run by one command, python3 -m unittest discover organize-downloads/tests, passing on Linux, and the macOS run by the user; no case's inputs or bars are written here (checked: discover finds test_*.py in that folder and runs them from the repository's root).

Each decision holds with every principle and every other line: both kinds of move never take a taken name and a failed copy adds no file, so nothing is overwritten or added; the record is started anew only by the first file a run moves, a kind's folder being recorded with the first file moved into it, so a run that moves no file, even one that made a kind's folder and then could not move into it, leaves the last move's record as it was, agreeing with the opening's 'the last run that moved a file in it', the why at lines 49-51, the tree's record line and the README's 'its last run that moved files in that folder'; the record is kept outside the folder; only the Planner decides where files go and the Mover is handed that same plan; the Undoer removes only kinds' folders the last move made, once empty; and the tests run on temporary folders, touching none of the user's files.

Each line is a decision whose change would change what is approved, said once: how files are moved, recorded and put back, where the record lives and how it is named, and how the tool is checked; the kinds, the extensions and the printed lines are left to the README it links, and how each case behaves to the tests.

Read once from the top, each line is understood where it is met: the README is linked for its terms such as a kind's folder, the five components keep one name each in the opening, the figure, the lines and the tree, a hard link is explained where it is first used, and each line rests only on what came before it.

chosen.chosen: The Mover moves a file by a hard link to its new name and then removing the old name, never by a rename.
chosen.why: A rename replaces a file that took the name after the Planner looked, while a hard link to a taken name fails and leaves both files, as checked with os.link and os.rename on a temporary folder, so the principle of never overwriting holds.

chosen.chosen: On a drive that cannot make hard links, the Mover makes the new name as a new file only where it is free, copies the contents, then removes the old name, and where the copy fails removes the new file and leaves the old one.
chosen.why: The README lets the user name any folder, such as one on a FAT or exFAT USB stick where hard links cannot be made; creating the file only where the name is free fails on a taken name, as checked with open in 'x' mode, so nothing is overwritten, and removing a failed copy adds no file, as AC7 asks.

chosen.chosen: The Mover has each file it moves added to the record as soon as it is moved, with the kind's folder it made if this is the first file in it, the first file moved in a run starting the folder's record anew.
chosen.why: A run stopped half way can still be undone, and a run that moves no file, even one that made a kind's folder and then could not move into it, leaves the last move's record for --undo, as the README's 'its last run that moved files in that folder' and G1's 'the last run that moved files' ask.

chosen.chosen: One record per folder, a JSON Lines file named by a hash of the folder's full path and holding that path, in organize-downloads/ under the place AC12 names.
chosen.why: A move in one folder never replaces another's record, a hash is always short enough for a file name, and a line written per move survives a run stopped half way.

chosen.chosen: Tests under organize-downloads/tests, one test_<component>.py per component and test_stories.py for the stories, run by python3 -m unittest discover organize-downloads/tests.
chosen.why: unittest's discover finds files named test_*.py with no setup, which gives the one command AC11 asks with nothing to install.
